answer: Under all-pairs echo enrollment, each new meadow identity must complete a unique timed challenge–response with every already-registered identity, so the echo grows linearly per existing node. An attacker fielding a hollow fleet of sybils pays a quadratic bill: joining 100 identities needs 100×99 = 9,900 distinct fresh handshakes, each with an unpredictable nonce and strict latency window that cannot be precomputed or replayed. A lone honest agent pays just one round of cheap local proofs against nearby peers, turning a relic of web-of-trust design into scalable identity minting.
